questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities? 1️⃣ The original Constitution of India did not make any provision with respect to this office. 2️⃣ The office was created based on the recommendation of the States Reorganisation Commission (1953-55). 3️⃣ The Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 inserted Article 350-B to provide for this office.
questions.e: Originally, the Constitution of India did not make any provision for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. Later, the States Reorganisation Commission (1953-55) made a recommendation in this regard. Accordingly, the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 inserted a new Article 350-B in Part XVII of the Constitution.

questions.q: With reference to the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities (CLM), consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The office was created in 1957 in pursuance of Article 350-B. 2️⃣ The CLM is appointed by the President of India. 3️⃣ The Commissioner falls under the Ministry of Home Affairs at the Central level.
questions.e: In pursuance of the provision of Article 350-B, the office was created in 1957 and the officer is appointed by the President. However, at the Central level, the CLM falls under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, not the Ministry of Home Affairs.

questions.q: Where is the headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities currently located?
questions.e: The Headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was established in 1957 at New Delhi. After a brief period, it was shifted to Allahabad and has been shifted back to New Delhi in 2015.

questions.q: Consider the following pairs regarding the regional offices of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities: 1️⃣ Belgaum: Karnataka 2️⃣ Chennai: Tamil Nadu 3️⃣ Kolkata: West Bengal. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The CLM has three regional offices located at Belgaum (Karnataka), Chennai (Tamil Nadu), and Kolkata (West Bengal). Each regional office is headed by an Assistant Commissioner.

questions.q: Which of the following details regarding the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are NOT specified by the Constitution of India? 1️⃣ Qualifications 2️⃣ Tenure 3️⃣ Salaries and allowances 4️⃣ Procedure for removal.
questions.e: The Constitution does not specify the qualifications, tenure, salaries and allowances, service conditions, and procedure for removal of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

questions.q: How is a 'linguistic minority' determined according to the provisions discussed in the text?
o: By the Ministry of Minority Affairs
questions.e: A linguistic minority is a group of people whose mother tongue is different from that of the majority in the state or part of a state. Thus, linguistic minorities are determined on a state-wise basis.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the reporting mechanism of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities: 1️⃣ The CLM submits annual reports to the President of India. 2️⃣ These reports are submitted through the Union Minority Affairs Minister. 3️⃣ The President must place these reports before each House of Parliament.
questions.e: The CLM submits annual reports or other reports to the President through the Union Minority Affairs Minister. The President should place all such reports before each House of Parliament and send them to the governments of the states concerned.

questions.q: What is the primary vision of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities as per the official mission statement?
o: To provide reserved seats in Parliament for linguistic minorities
To replace English with regional languages in high courts
Streamlining and strengthening implementation machinery for effective implementation of Constitutional safeguards
To promote the use of Hindi in all states
questions.e: The vision of the CLM is streamlining and strengthening implementation machinery and mechanism for effective implementation of the Constitutional safeguards for the Linguistic Minorities, ensuring protection of rights and equal opportunities.

questions.q: Which of the following are listed as objectives of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities? 1️⃣ To provide equal opportunities for inclusive development and national integration. 2️⃣ To spread awareness amongst linguistic minorities about available safeguards. 3️⃣ To handle representations for redress of grievances related to safeguards.
questions.e: The objectives include providing equal opportunities for inclusive development, spreading awareness about safeguards, ensuring effective implementation of safeguards provided in the Constitution, and handling representations for redress of grievances.

questions.q: Who assists the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities at the headquarters?
o: A Deputy Commissioner and an Assistant Commissioner
A team of five Regional Directors
questions.e: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities (CLM) is assisted at the headquarters by a Deputy Commissioner and an Assistant Commissioner.

questions.q: With reference to the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 148 provides for an independent office of the CAG. 2️⃣ The CAG is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department. 3️⃣ The CAG is the guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system at both Centre and State levels.
questions.e: Article 148 of the Constitution provides for an independent office of the CAG. He/she is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department and the guardian of the public purse, controlling the financial system at both the Centre and State levels.

questions.q: Who described the CAG as 'the most important Officer under the Constitution of India'?
questions.e: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar said that the CAG shall be the most important Officer under the Constitution of India, describing it as one of the bulwarks of the democratic system.

questions.q: According to the Constitution, which of the following are considered 'bulwarks' of the democratic system of government in India? 1️⃣ Supreme Court 2️⃣ Election Commission 3️⃣ Union Public Service Commission 4️⃣ Comptroller and Auditor General.
questions.e: The CAG is one of the bulwarks of the democratic system of government in India, with the others being the Supreme Court, the Election Commission, and the Union Public Service Commission.

questions.q: How is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India appointed?
o: By the Parliament through a resolution
By the President of India by a warrant under his/her hand and seal
By the Chief Justice of India
questions.e: The CAG is appointed by the President of India by a warrant under his/her hand and seal.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
questions.e: The CAG holds office for a period of six years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the removal of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India?
o: He/she can be removed by a simple majority resolution in the Lok Sabha.
He/she holds office during the pleasure of the President.
He/she can be removed by the Prime Minister for misbehaviour.
He/she can be removed by the President on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court.
questions.e: The CAG does not hold office till the pleasure of the President. He/she can be removed by the President only on the same grounds and in the same manner as a judge of the Supreme Court, which requires a special majority in both Houses.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a provision to safeguard the independence of the CAG?
o: He/she is provided with security of tenure.
The administrative expenses of the office of the CAG are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.
His/her salary and service conditions are determined by the President and can be changed to his/her disadvantage.
He/she is not eligible for further office under the Government of India or any State after retirement.
questions.e: The conditions of service of the CAG cannot be varied to his/her disadvantage after appointment. Other points like security of tenure and ineligibility for further office are constitutional safeguards for independence.

questions.q: In 1976, the CAG was relieved of which of the following responsibilities?
o: Auditing the accounts of the State Governments
Compilation and maintenance of accounts of the Central Government
questions.e: In 1976, the CAG was relieved of responsibilities with regard to the compilation and maintenance of accounts of the Central Government due to the separation of accounts from audit (departmentalisation of accounts).

questions.q: To whom does the CAG submit the audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The CAG submits three audit reports to the President: audit report on appropriation accounts, audit report on finance accounts, and audit report on public undertakings.

questions.q: Which committee of the Parliament examines the audit reports of the CAG?
questions.e: After the President lays the CAG's reports before both Houses of Parliament, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) examines them and reports its findings to the Parliament.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Legal and regulatory audit is obligatory for the CAG. 2️⃣ Propriety audit is discretionary for the CAG. 3️⃣ In 2006, it was clarified that performance audit falls within the scope of CAG's audit. Which of the above are correct?
questions.e: Legal and regulatory audit is obligatory. The CAG can also conduct propriety audit (looking into wisdom/economy), which is discretionary. In 2006, the Ministry of Finance clarified that performance audit is also within the scope of CAG's audit.

questions.q: What is the main difference between the CAG of India and the CAG of Britain?
o: The CAG of India is a member of the Cabinet, unlike in Britain.
The CAG of India acts only as an Auditor-General, whereas the CAG of Britain has powers of both Comptroller and Auditor General.
The CAG of India is not an independent office.
The CAG of Britain is appointed for life.
questions.e: In India, the CAG has no control over the issue of money from the consolidated fund and acts primarily at the audit stage. In Britain, the executive can draw money only with the approval of the CAG, who fulfills both Comptroller and Auditor roles.

questions.q: With reference to the audit of public corporations by the CAG, which category is correctly described?
o: The CAG has no role in auditing any public corporation.
All public corporations are audited exclusively by private auditors.
Private auditors are appointed for corporations without consulting the CAG.
Some corporations are audited totally and directly by the CAG.
questions.e: Relationship with public corporations falls into three categories: (i) some audited totally/directly by CAG, (ii) some audited by private auditors in consultation with CAG, and (iii) some subjected totally to private audit where the CAG does not come into the picture.

questions.q: Who is known as the 'guide, friend and philosopher' of the Public Accounts Committee?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The CAG acts as a guide, friend, and philosopher of the Public Accounts Committee of the Parliament.

questions.q: Who was the American scholar critical of the role of the CAG in India and recommended the abolition of the office?
questions.e: Paul H. Appleby, in his reports on Indian Administration, was very critical of the CAG, suggesting the office be relieved of audit responsibilities or even abolished.

questions.q: Which of the following is a limitation on the auditing role of the CAG as mentioned in the text?
o: Auditing the accounts of State Governments
Auditing the accounts of the Supreme Court
questions.e: The secret service expenditure is a limitation on the auditing role of the CAG. He cannot call for particulars but must accept a certificate from the competent administrative authority that expenditure was incurred.

questions.q: According to the Second Administrative Reforms Commission, what percentage of audit paras in the CAG reports are typically examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) every year?
o: Only the paras relating to the Ministry of Home Affairs
questions.e: The Second ARC noted that detailed examination by the PAC is barely about 15-20 paras against the total of 1000 to 1500 paras included in the CAG's reports submitted annually.

questions.q: Match the following Articles with their subjects: 1️⃣ Article 148: CAG of India 2️⃣ Article 149: Duties and powers of CAG 3️⃣ Article 151: Audit reports. How many are correctly matched?
questions.e: Table 52.1 lists Article 148 (CAG of India), Article 149 (Duties and powers of CAG), Article 150 (Form of accounts of Union and States), and Article 151 (Audit reports).

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the office of the Attorney General of India?
questions.e: Article 76 of the Constitution of India provides for the office of the Attorney General (AG) for India.

questions.q: What are the qualifications required to be appointed as the Attorney General of India?
o: He/she must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court.
He/she must be a member of the Lok Sabha.
He/she must be a retired Chief Justice of India.
He/she must be a judge of a High Court for 10 years.
questions.e: The AG must be a person who is qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court. This means being a citizen of India and having been a judge of a High Court for 5 years, or an advocate of a High Court for 10 years, or an eminent jurist.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the term of the Attorney General of India: 1️⃣ The term of office is fixed at 6 years by the Constitution. 2️⃣ The Constitution does not contain the procedure for his/her removal. 3️⃣ He/she holds office during the pleasure of the President. Which of the above are correct?
questions.e: The term of office of the AG is not fixed by the Constitution. He/she holds office during the pleasure of the President and can be removed at any time. The Constitution does not specify removal procedures or grounds.

questions.q: Which of the following is a right of the Attorney General of India? 1️⃣ Right of audience in all courts in India. 2️⃣ Right to speak and take part in proceedings of both Houses of Parliament. 3️⃣ Right to vote in the proceedings of Parliament.
questions.e: The AG has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India. He/she also has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses or their joint sittings, but without a right to vote.

questions.q: Which of the following limitations are placed on the Attorney General? 1️⃣ He/she should not advise against the Government of India. 2️⃣ He/she should not defend accused persons in criminal cases without Government permission. 3️⃣ He/she is debarred from private legal practice.
questions.e: Limitations include not advising against the GOI and not defending accused in criminal cases without permission. However, the AG is NOT debarred from private legal practice as he/she is not a full-time government servant.

questions.q: Who assists the Attorney General of India in his/her official responsibilities? 1️⃣ Solicitor General of India 2️⃣ Additional Solicitor General of India 3️⃣ Law Minister.
questions.e: The Solicitor General of India and the Additional Solicitor General of India assist the AG. The Law Minister is a separate member of the Central cabinet.

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding the Solicitor General of India?
o: The office is created by Article 76 of the Constitution.
The Solicitor General is the highest law officer in the country.
The Solicitor General has the right to vote in Parliament.
The office is not mentioned in the Constitution.
questions.e: Only the office of the AG is created by the Constitution. Article 76 does not mention the solicitor general or additional solicitor general.

questions.q: Match the following Articles related to the Attorney General: 1️⃣ Article 76: AG of India 2️⃣ Article 88: Rights of AG as respects Houses of Parliament 3️⃣ Article 105: Powers, privileges and immunities of AG. How many pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: Table 53.1 lists Article 76 (AG of India), Article 88 (Rights regarding Houses of Parliament), and Article 105 (Powers, privileges and immunities).

questions.q: Which Article provides for the office of the Advocate General of the State?
questions.e: Article 165 of the Constitution provides for the office of the advocate general for the states.

questions.q: Who appoints the Advocate General of a State?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The advocate general is appointed by the governor of the state.

questions.q: What is the qualification for the appointment of the Advocate General of a State?
o: Must have been a member of the State Legislature
Must have 15 years of experience as a district judge
Qualified to be a judge of a High Court
Qualified to be a judge of the Supreme Court
questions.e: The advocate general must be a person who is qualified to be appointed as a judge of a High Court.

questions.q: Consider the following regarding the Advocate General of the State: 1️⃣ The term of office is 5 years. 2️⃣ He/she holds office during the pleasure of the Governor. 3️⃣ He/she can take part in the proceedings of the state legislature without a right to vote. Which are correct?
questions.e: The term is not fixed by the Constitution. He/she holds office during the pleasure of the governor. He/she has the right to speak and take part in proceedings of the state legislature but without a right to vote.

questions.q: To whom does the Advocate General submit his/her resignation?
questions.e: The advocate general may quit office by submitting his/her resignation to the governor.

questions.q: Which of the following Constitutional Bodies is matched with its correct Article? 1️⃣ State Finance Commission: Article 243-I 2️⃣ Inter-State Council: Article 263 3️⃣ Finance Commission: Article 280 4️⃣ Election Commission: Article 324.
questions.e: Table 54.2 lists these bodies: State Finance Commission (243-I), Inter-State Council (263), Finance Commission (280), and Election Commission (324).

questions.q: Which Article deals with the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC)?
questions.e: Article 338B deals with the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC).

questions.q: Who determines the composition of the Inter-State Council?
o: The Chief Ministers of all states
questions.e: According to Table 55.1, the composition of the Inter-State Council (Article 263) is determined by the President.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of members prescribed for the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim?
questions.e: According to Table 55.1 (item 36), the minimum number of members for the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim is 30.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chairman and Members of a State Public Service Commission (SPSC)?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: According to Table 55.2 (item 30), the Chairman and Members of a SPSC are appointed by the Governor.

questions.q: Who is the appointing authority for the Chief Minister of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi?
o: The Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court
questions.e: According to Table 55.2 (item 23), the Chief Minister of NCT of Delhi is appointed by the President.

questions.q: What is the prescribed age for the retirement of a judge of the High Court?
questions.e: According to Table 55.3 (item 9), the retirement age of a judge of the High Courts is 62 years.

questions.q: What is the minimum age required for election to the Rajya Sabha?
questions.e: According to Table 55.3 (item 3), the prescribed age for election as a member of the Rajya Sabha is 30 years.

questions.q: Who administers the oath to the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: According to Table 55.4 (item 7), the oath of the CAG is made and subscribed before the President (or some person appointed in that behalf by him).

questions.q: Who administers the oath of office to the Governor of a State?
o: The Chief Justice of the State High Court
questions.e: According to Table 55.4 (item 8), the oath of a Governor is made before the Chief Justice of the State High Court (or the senior most Judge of the State High Court available).

questions.q: Which of the following functionaries hold office during the pleasure of the President? 1️⃣ Prime Minister 2️⃣ Attorney-General 3️⃣ Governor 4️⃣ CAG.
questions.e: According to Table 55.5, the Prime Minister, Central Ministers, AG, and Governor hold office during the pleasure of the President. The CAG's term is determined by Parliament and they have security of tenure.

questions.q: Who determines the salary of the Advocate-General of a State?
questions.e: According to Table 55.6 (item 14), the salary of the Advocate-General of a State is determined by the Governor.

questions.q: To whom does the Speaker of the Lok Sabha submit his/her resignation?
o: The Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: According to Table 55.7 (item 4), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha submits his/her resignation to the Deputy Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Who is the authority empowered to remove a judge of the High Court?
o: The President on the recommendation of the Parliament
questions.e: According to Table 55.8 (item 13), judges of the High Courts are removed by the President on the recommendation of the Parliament.

questions.q: To whom does the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (STs) submit its report?
questions.e: According to Table 55.9 (item 10), the National Commission for STs submits its report to the President.

questions.q: When was the NITI Aayog established?
questions.e: The NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was established on January 1, 2015, as the successor to the Planning Commission.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the nature of NITI Aayog?
o: It is a non-constitutional and non-statutory body.
questions.e: NITI Aayog was created by an executive resolution of the Government of India. It is neither a constitutional body nor a statutory body. It is an extra-constitutional or non-constitutional body.

questions.q: What is the primary role of NITI Aayog for the Government of India?
o: Acting as the executive authority for resource allocation
Serving as a premier policy 'Think Tank'
questions.e: NITI Aayog is the premier policy 'Think Tank' of the Government of India, providing both directional and policy inputs.

questions.q: NITI Aayog's policy thinking is shaped by which of the following approaches?
questions.e: In the spirit of federalism, NITI's policy thinking is shaped by a 'bottom-up' approach rather than a 'top-down' model.

questions.q: Who is the Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
questions.e: The Chairperson of NITI Aayog is the Prime Minister of India.

questions.q: Who comprises the Governing Council of NITI Aayog?
o: The Prime Minister and Vice-Chairperson only
Chief Ministers of all States and Lt. Governors of UTs
questions.e: The Governing Council comprises the Chief Ministers of all the States, Chief Ministers of UTs with Legislatures (Delhi, Puducherry, Jammu and Kashmir), and Lt. Governors of other UTs.

questions.q: How is the Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog appointed?
questions.e: The Vice-Chairperson of NITI Aayog is appointed by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: What is the rank enjoyed by the Full-time Members of NITI Aayog?
o: Secretary to the Government of India
questions.e: According to the organisational framework, Full-time Members enjoy the rank of a Minister of State.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of ex-officio members from the Union Council of Ministers that can be nominated to NITI Aayog?
questions.e: A maximum of 4 members of the Union Council of Ministers can be nominated by the Prime Minister as ex-officio members of NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Which of the following are the two main hubs through which NITI Aayog functions?
o: Team India and Knowledge and Innovation
questions.e: NITI Aayog's entire gamut of activities is divided into two main hubs: Team India Hub and Knowledge and Innovation Hub.

questions.q: Which of the following principles guides NITI Aayog's activities? 1️⃣ Antyodaya 2️⃣ Inclusion 3️⃣ Village 4️⃣ Demographic Dividend.
questions.e: NITI Aayog is guided by principles including Antyodaya (uplift of poor), Inclusion, Village (integrating villages), Demographic Dividend, People’s Participation, Governance, and Sustainability.

questions.q: How does NITI Aayog promote 'Competitive Federalism'?
o: By taking over state administrations during emergencies
By allocating more funds to the ruling party's states
Through transparent rankings of states in various sectors
By providing mandatory orders to state governments
questions.e: NITI Aayog promotes competitive federalism by facilitating improved performance of States/UTs through transparent rankings in various sectors (like School Education, Health, etc.) along with a hand-holding approach.

questions.q: Consider the following indices launched by NITI Aayog: 1️⃣ School Education Quality Index 2️⃣ State Health Index 3️⃣ Composite Water Management Index 4️⃣ India Innovation Index. Which of these are correct?
questions.e: The text lists several indices launched by NITI Aayog to promote competitive federalism, including School Education Quality Index, State Health Index, Composite Water Management Index, SDG Index, India Innovation Index, and Export Competitiveness Index.

questions.q: Which autonomous body supports NITI Aayog and was formerly known as the Institute of Applied Manpower Research (IAMR)?
questions.e: The National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD), formerly IAMR, is a central autonomous organization under NITI Aayog.

questions.q: What is the primary role of the Development Monitoring and Evaluation Office (DMEO)?
o: To allocate funds to different ministries
To conduct elections in various states
To support the government through monitoring and evaluation of policies and programs
To provide legal advice to the Prime Minister
questions.e: DMEO was established in 2015 as an attached office of NITI Aayog to support the Government through monitoring and evaluation of government policies and programs to achieve the national development agenda.

questions.q: When was the erstwhile Planning Commission established?
questions.e: The erstwhile Planning Commission was established in March 1950 by an executive resolution of the Government of India.

questions.q: Who was the chairman of the Advisory Planning Board on whose recommendation the Planning Commission was established?
questions.e: The Planning Commission was established on the recommendation of the Advisory Planning Board constituted in 1946 under the chairmanship of K.C. Neogi.

questions.q: Which of the following terms was used by critics to describe the erstwhile Planning Commission?
questions.e: Critics described the Planning Commission as a 'Super Cabinet', an 'Economic Cabinet', a 'Parallel Cabinet', and the 'Fifth Wheel of the Coach'.

questions.q: When was the National Development Council (NDC) established?
questions.e: The National Development Council (NDC) was established in August 1952 by an executive resolution of the Government of India.

questions.q: Who are the members of the National Development Council (NDC)? 1️⃣ Prime Minister 2️⃣ All Union Cabinet Ministers 3️⃣ Chief Ministers of all states 4️⃣ Members of NITI Aayog.
questions.e: The NDC is composed of the Prime Minister, all Union Cabinet Ministers (since 1967), Chief Ministers of all states and UTs, and members of the Planning Commission (now NITI Aayog).

questions.q: Which body was described by K. Santhanam as having 'superseded the federation'?
questions.e: Eminent constitutional expert K. Santhanam stated that 'Planning has superseded the federation and our country is functioning like a unitary system in many respects', referring to the role of the Planning Commission.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is which type of body?
questions.e: The National Human Rights Commission is a statutory body, established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act.

questions.q: Who appoints the chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission?
o: The President on the recommendation of a six-member committee
questions.e: The chairperson and members of the NHRC are appointed by the President on the recommendations of a six-member committee.

questions.q: Who is the head of the committee that recommends appointments to the NHRC?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The six-member committee for NHRC appointments is headed by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a member of the committee that recommends appointments to the NHRC?
o: Leader of the Opposition in Lok Sabha
Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: The committee consists of the PM (head), Speaker of Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, leaders of the Opposition in both Houses, and the Central Home Minister. The CJI is not a member, though he is consulted for appointing sitting judges.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the chairperson and members of the NHRC after the 2019 amendment?
questions.e: Following the 2019 Amendment Act, the term of the chairperson and members of the NHRC was reduced from five to three years, or until they attain the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

questions.q: Which of the following is true regarding the eligibility for re-appointment of NHRC members?
o: They are not eligible for re-appointment.
Only the chairperson is eligible for re-appointment.
They can only be re-appointed once.
questions.e: The chairperson and members of the NHRC are eligible for re-appointment.

questions.q: On what grounds can the President remove the NHRC chairperson or members? 1️⃣ Adjudged insolvent 2️⃣ Paid employment outside duties 3️⃣ Unfit due to infirmity of mind or body 4️⃣ Proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
questions.e: The President can remove them if they are insolvent, engaged in outside paid employment, unfit due to infirmity, of unsound mind, or convicted for an offence. Removal for proved misbehaviour or incapacity requires a Supreme Court inquiry.

questions.q: The NHRC can inquire into human rights violations within what period of their occurrence?
questions.e: The commission is not empowered to inquire into any matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act of violation is alleged to have been committed.

questions.q: Which of the following is correct regarding the nature of NHRC's recommendations?
o: They are mainly recommendatory in nature.
They can be challenged only in the Supreme Court.
They are binding on the government.
They must be implemented within 15 days.
questions.e: The functions of the NHRC are mainly recommendatory in nature. It has no power to punish violators or award relief; its recommendations are not binding on the government.

questions.q: With respect to human rights violations by members of the armed forces, what is the role of the NHRC?
o: It has no jurisdiction over the armed forces.
It has full power to prosecute the soldiers.
It can only seek a report from the Central government and make recommendations.
It can conduct its own independent field investigation.
questions.e: The commission has a limited role with respect to the armed forces. It may seek a report from the Central government and then make its recommendations.

questions.q: Who determines the salaries and allowances of the NHRC chairperson and members?
questions.e: The salaries, allowances, and other conditions of service of the NHRC chairperson or members are determined by the Central government.

questions.q: A State Human Rights Commission can inquire into violation of human rights in respect of subjects mentioned in which list(s)?
questions.e: A State Human Rights Commission can inquire into violation of human rights only in respect of subjects mentioned in the State List (List-II) and the Concurrent List (List-III).

questions.q: Who appoints the chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission?
questions.e: The chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission are appointed by the Governor.

questions.q: Although appointed by the Governor, who has the power to remove the chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission?
questions.e: Although the chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission are appointed by the governor, they can be removed only by the President.

questions.q: After the 2019 amendment, who is eligible to be appointed as the Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission? 1️⃣ Retired Chief Justice of a High Court 2️⃣ Retired Judge of a High Court 3️⃣ Retired Judge of the Supreme Court.
questions.e: The 2019 Amendment Act provided that a person who has been a judge of a High Court is also made eligible to be appointed as Chairperson of the State Human Rights Commission, in addition to the person who has been the Chief Justice of a High Court.

questions.q: Who is responsible for dealing with human rights violations in the Union Territory of Delhi?
o: State Human Rights Commission of Delhi
questions.e: The 2019 amendment provided that the functions relating to human rights in the case of the union territory of Delhi are to be dealt with by the National Human Rights Commission.

questions.q: Who provides concurrence for the establishment of Human Rights Courts in every district?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court of that state
questions.e: Human Rights Courts can be set up by the state government only with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court of that state.

questions.q: When was the National Commission for Women (NCW) established?
questions.e: The National Commission for Women was constituted in 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.

questions.q: Which ministry is the nodal ministry for the National Commission for Women?
o: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
Ministry of Women and Child Development
questions.e: The Ministry of Women and Child Development of the Government of India is the nodal ministry for the National Commission for Women.

questions.q: What is the composition of the National Commission for Women?
o: A Chairperson, 5 members, and a member-secretary
questions.e: The Commission is a multi-member body consisting of a chairperson, five members, and a member-secretary.

questions.q: At least one member each of the National Commission for Women should belong to which category?
questions.e: According to the NCW composition rules, at least one member each should belong to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, respectively.

questions.q: How long is the term of office for the chairperson and members of the National Commission for Women?
questions.e: The chairperson and members of the National Commission for Women hold office for three years.

questions.q: To whom does the National Commission for Women submit its annual report?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: The Commission presents an annual report to the Central Government, which then places it before each House of Parliament.

questions.q: Which innovative concept was evolved by the NCW for speedy disposal of matters related to marriage and family affairs?
questions.e: The Commission evolved the concept of Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat (PMLA) to supplement the efforts of District Legal Service Authority for redressal of marriage and family disputes.

questions.q: The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) was set up in which year?
questions.e: NCPCR was set up in 2007 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.

questions.q: Under the NCPCR Act, what is the defined age of a 'child'?
questions.e: Under the UN Convention ratified by India and used by NCPCR, a child is defined as a human being below the age of eighteen years.

questions.q: How many members of the NCPCR must be women?
questions.e: The Commission consists of a Chairperson and six members. Out of the six members, at least two should be women.

questions.q: What is the upper age limit for the Chairperson of the NCPCR?
questions.e: According to the Act, the upper age limit for holding office as Chairperson is 65 years, and for members, it is 60 years.

questions.q: How many terms can a person hold office in the NCPCR?
questions.e: The Chairperson and members hold office for a term of three years and are not eligible for appointment for more than two terms.

questions.q: The NCPCR has been assigned additional functions under which of the following Acts? 1️⃣ RTE Act, 2009 2️⃣ POCSO Act, 2012 3️⃣ Juvenile Justice Act, 2015.
questions.e: The Commission performs additional functions under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009; the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012; and the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection) Act, 2015.

questions.q: Who appoints the chairperson of the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The chairperson and other members of the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights are appointed by the state government.

questions.q: What type of court can be specified as a Children's Court for speedy trials?
questions.e: The state government may specify for each district a Court of Session to be a Children's Court for the speedy trial of offences against children.

questions.q: Which article mentions the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
questions.e: Article 350-B in Part XVII of the Constitution contains the provisions for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

questions.q: With reference to the removal of the CAG, consider the following statements: 1️⃣ He/she is removed by the President. 2️⃣ A resolution must be passed by both Houses of Parliament. 3️⃣ The resolution must be passed by a simple majority. Which of the above are correct?
questions.e: The CAG is removed by the President on the basis of a resolution passed by both Houses of Parliament with a special majority (not simple majority) on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

questions.q: The CAG does not audit the accounts of which of the following?
questions.e: While the CAG audits Centre and State accounts, his role in local bodies is not direct unless requested or specified by law. His primary mandate covers Central and State governments and certain corporations.

questions.q: Who determines the salaries of the Judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.e: According to Table 55.6 (item 9), the salary of the Judges of the Supreme Court is determined by the Parliament.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.e: Finance Commission, Election Commission, and UPSC are mentioned in the Constitution. NITI Aayog was created by an executive resolution and is a non-constitutional body.

questions.q: To whom does the Vice-President of India submit his/her resignation?
o: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.e: According to Table 55.7 (item 2), the Vice-President submits his/her resignation to the President.

questions.q: Which Article empowers the CAG to audit the accounts of the Union and of the States?
questions.e: Article 149 deals with the duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

questions.q: Who determines the term and service conditions of the Chief Election Commissioner (subject to law of Parliament)?
questions.e: According to Table 55.5 (item 24), the term of the Chief Election Commissioner and other election Commissioners is determined by the President (subject to the law of Parliament).

questions.q: Which body is responsible for providing technical advice to the Centre and States on strategic and long-term policies?
questions.e: While designing strategic and long-term policies, NITI Aayog provides relevant technical advice to the Centre and States.

questions.q: Which hub of NITI Aayog maintains a repository of research on good governance?
questions.e: The Knowledge and Innovation Hub maintains a state-of-the-art resource centre and a repository of research on good governance and best practices.

questions.q: In 1976, the separation of accounts from audit led to the 'departmentalisation of accounts' for which level of government?
questions.e: In 1976, the CAG was relieved of responsibilities for compilation and maintenance of accounts for the Central Government due to departmentalisation of accounts. He still maintains accounts for State governments.

questions.q: Who is the de facto executive head of the erstwhile Planning Commission?
questions.e: The Prime Minister was the chairman, but the Deputy Chairman was the de facto executive head (full-time functional head) of the commission.

questions.q: The Protection of Human Rights Act was enacted in which year?
questions.e: The National Human Rights Commission was established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.q: After the 2019 amendment, a woman member in NHRC is:
questions.e: The 2019 Amendment Act increased the number of members from person having practical experience from two to three, out of which at least one has to be a woman.

questions.q: Which of the following can the NHRC recommend after an inquiry? 1️⃣ Payment of compensation 2️⃣ Prosecution of guilty public servant 3️⃣ Grant of immediate interim relief.
questions.e: Upon completion of an inquiry, the NHRC can recommend compensation, prosecution of guilty servants, and grant of interim relief.

questions.q: What is the upper age limit for holding office as a member of the NCPCR?
questions.e: According to the text, the upper age limit for members of the NCPCR is 60 years.

questions.q: To whom does the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities submit annual reports?
questions.e: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities reports to the President upon those matters at such intervals as the President may direct.

questions.q: Which Article specifies that the CAG's administrative expenses are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India?
questions.e: Article 148 contains the provisions that safeguard the independence of the CAG, including that administrative expenses are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India.

questions.q: Who was the first Prime Minister to propose merging the office of Attorney General with the Law Minister?
questions.e: During the prime ministership of Jawaharlal Nehru, a proposal was put forward that the office of the Attorney General be merged with the office of the law minister, but it did not materialise.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the rights of the Attorney General as respects the Houses of Parliament?
questions.e: Table 53.1 lists Article 88 as the one dealing with the rights of the Attorney-General as respects the Houses of Parliament and its Committee.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Body’s composition is determined by the state legislature?
questions.e: According to Table 55.1 (item 11), the composition of Panchayats (Article 243C) is determined by the State Legislature.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to be registered as a voter in India?
questions.e: According to Table 55.3 (item 15), registration as a voter in the electoral roll (Article 326) requires a prescribed age of 18 years.

questions.q: Which body is described as the 'premier policy Think Tank' of the Government of India?
questions.e: The NITI Aayog is the premier policy 'Think Tank' of the Government of India, providing both directional and policy inputs.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'guiding principle' of NITI Aayog related to the uplift of the poor?
questions.e: Antyodaya means to prioritise service and uplift of the poor, marginalised and downtrodden, as enunciated in Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's idea.

questions.q: What is the tenure of the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of NITI Aayog?
questions.e: The Chief Executive Officer is appointed by the Prime Minister for a fixed tenure, in the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

questions.q: In which year did the headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities shift back to New Delhi?
questions.e: The Headquarters was shifted back to New Delhi in 2015 from Allahabad.

questions.q: Who has the power to remove the chairperson of the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights?
o: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.e: The state government can remove the chairperson from their office on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the Finance Commission of India?
questions.e: Article 280 of the Constitution deals with the Finance Commission.

questions.q: Who is the appointing authority for District Judges?
o: The Chief Justice of High Court
questions.e: According to Table 55.2 (item 21), District Judges (Article 233) are appointed by the Governor.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "Audit Reports" of the CAG?
questions.e: Article 151 of the Constitution deals with the audit reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

questions.q: The 'Secret Service Expenditure' audit by CAG is:
o: Done with the help of private auditors
questions.e: The secret service expenditure is a limitation on the auditing role of the CAG. He has to accept a certificate from the competent administrative authority.

questions.q: Who is the 'highest law officer' in a State?
questions.e: The Advocate General (Article 165) is the highest law officer in the state.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the "Election Commission" of India?
questions.e: Article 324 of the Constitution provides for the Election Commission.

questions.q: What is the term of the President of India?
questions.e: According to Table 55.5 (item 1), the term of the President is 5 years.

questions.q: Who determines the salary of the Governor of a state?
questions.e: According to Table 55.6 (item 11), the salary of the Governor of a state is determined by the Parliament.

questions.q: To whom does the Governor submit his/her resignation?
questions.e: According to Table 55.7 (item 9), the Governor of a state submits his/her resignation to the President.

questions.q: Which body is NOT subject to dissolution?
questions.e: According to Table 55.8 (item 3), the Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution; it is a continuing chamber.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council?
questions.e: According to Table 55.1 (item 18), the GST Council consists of a Chairperson (Union Finance Minister), Vice-Chairperson, and Members.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "Official Language Commission"?
questions.e: Article 344 deals with the Official Language Commission and Official Language Committee of Parliament.

questions.q: Who appoints the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities?
questions.e: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President of India.

questions.q: What is the minimum age for election as a member of the Lok Sabha?
questions.e: According to Table 55.3 (item 4), the prescribed age for election as a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "Forms of accounts of the Union and of the States"?
questions.e: Article 150 of the Constitution deals with the form of accounts of the Union and of the States.

questions.q: To whom does the Chairperson of the District Planning Committee submit the report?
questions.e: According to Table 55.9 (item 3), the Chairperson of the District Planning Committee submits the report to the State Government.

questions.q: The NITI Aayog was established as the successor to which body?
questions.e: On January 1, 2015, the NITI Aayog was established as the successor to the Planning Commission.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'non-constitutional body' listed in the text?
questions.e: The text in Part VIII lists non-constitutional bodies including NITI Aayog, NHRC, CBI, etc.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
questions.e: The composition of NITI Aayog includes the Prime Minister of India as the Chairperson.

questions.q: Which principle of NITI Aayog focuses on harnessing India's youth through education and skilling?
questions.e: Demographic dividend involves harnessing the people of India by focussing on their development through education and skilling.

questions.q: The DMEO was formed by merging which two offices?
o: Programme Evaluation Organization and Independent Evaluation Office
NITI Hub and Team India Hub
questions.e: The DMEO was established in 2015 by merging the erstwhile Programme Evaluation Organization and the Independent Evaluation Office.

questions.q: What is the term of office for NHRC members after the 2019 amendment?
questions.e: Following the 2019 amendment, the term was reduced from five years to three years.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio member of NHRC from the National Commission for BCs?
questions.e: Following the 2019 amendment, the Chairpersons of various commissions, including the National Commission for BCs, are ex-officio members of the NHRC.

questions.q: To whom does the NCW submit its annual report?
questions.e: The NCW presents an annual report to the Central Government.

questions.q: What is the upper age limit for members of the NCPCR?
questions.e: The upper age limit for members of the NCPCR is 60 years, while for the Chairperson, it is 65 years.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the "Attorney General of India"?
questions.e: Article 76 provides for the office of the Attorney General of India.

questions.q: The salary of the CAG is equal to that of:
o: A Judge of the Supreme Court
questions.e: Although not explicitly in the summary, the independence provisions imply his status is aligned with Supreme Court judges. Table 55.6 notes his salary is determined by Parliament, similar to SC judges.

questions.q: Who can remove the Attorney General of India?
questions.e: The AG holds office during the pleasure of the President, meaning the President can remove him at any time.

questions.q: Which Article is related to the "Advocate-General of the State"?
questions.e: Article 165 provides for the office of the advocate general for the states.

questions.q: The minimum age for becoming a member of a Panchayat is:
questions.e: According to Table 55.3 (item 10), the prescribed age for election as a member of the Panchayats is 21 years.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
questions.e: The Chief Election Commissioner and other election Commissioners are appointed by the President.

questions.q: NITI Aayog follows which approach in its policy thinking?
questions.e: In the spirit of federalism, NITI's policy thinking is shaped by a 'bottom-up' approach.

questions.q: Which body acts as the 'watchdog of human rights' in India?
questions.e: The NHRC is described as the watchdog of human rights in the country.

questions.q: Who is the current Chairperson of NITI Aayog?
questions.e: The Prime Minister of India is the ex-officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

questions.q: The "Team India Hub" in NITI Aayog focuses on:
questions.e: The Team India Hub carries out the mandate of fostering cooperative federalism and engagement with States.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the "Comptroller and Auditor-General of India"?
questions.e: Article 148 provides for an independent office of the CAG.

questions.q: Who is the 'highest law officer' in India?
questions.e: The Attorney General (Article 76) is the highest law officer in the country.

questions.q: The "Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat" is an initiative of:
questions.e: The NCW evolved the concept of Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat for speedy disposal of family disputes.

questions.q: What is the term of a member of the UPSC?
questions.e: According to Table 55.3 and 55.5, the retirement age for a UPSC member is 65, and the term is 6 years.

questions.q: Who determines the salary of the CAG?
questions.e: The salary and other conditions of service of the CAG are determined by the Parliament.

questions.q: Which Article is related to the "National Commission for Scheduled Castes"?
questions.e: Article 338 deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.

questions.q: The NITI Aayog was established via:
questions.e: NITI Aayog was created by an executive resolution of the Government of India.

questions.q: Who is the 'guardian of the public purse' in India?
questions.e: The CAG is the guardian of the public purse and controls the entire financial system.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "Rights of Attorney-General in Parliament"?
questions.e: Article 88 provides the AG with the right to speak and participate in Parliament proceedings.

questions.q: The "Antyodaya" principle means:
o: Uplift of the poor and marginalised
questions.e: Antyodaya involves prioritising service and uplift of the poor and marginalised.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chairperson of the NHRC?
questions.e: The President appoints the NHRC Chairperson on the recommendation of a committee.

questions.q: Which of the following is a limitation of the CAG's audit?
questions.e: Secret service expenditure is a limitation on the auditing role of the CAG.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the Advocate General of a State?
questions.e: The term of office of the advocate general is not fixed by the Constitution.

questions.q: The National Commission for Women was established in which year?
questions.e: The National Commission for Women was constituted in 1992.

questions.q: Who is the head of the "Team India Hub" in NITI Aayog?
questions.e: As Chairperson, the PM heads the overall NITI Aayog structure including its hubs.

questions.q: The "Demographic Dividend" refers to:
o: Economic growth potential of the working-age population
questions.e: In the context of NITI Aayog, it refers to harnessing the potential of India's youth asset through skilling.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "National Commission for Scheduled Tribes"?
questions.e: Article 338A deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

questions.q: Who determines the salary of the Advocate General of a State?
questions.e: The Advocate General receives such remuneration as the governor may determine.

questions.q: The CAG can conduct 'Propriety Audit' which is:
questions.e: The propriety audit is discretionary, unlike the legal and regulatory audit which is obligatory.

questions.q: The NITI Aayog replaced which of the following?
questions.e: NITI Aayog was established as the successor to the Planning Commission.

questions.q: Which body is the 'watchdog of human rights' at the state level?
questions.e: The State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) is the state-level watchdog.

questions.q: Who appoints the judges of the Supreme Court?
questions.e: Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed by the President.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities"?
questions.e: Article 350-B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.

questions.q: The NHRC consists of a chairperson and how many full-time members?
questions.e: The commission consists of a chairperson and five full-time members.

questions.q: Who appoints the Advocate General of a State?
o: The Chief Justice of High Court
questions.e: The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'constitutional body'?
questions.e: UPSC is a constitutional body (Article 315).

questions.q: The NCW consists of a chairperson and how many members?
questions.e: The NCW consists of a chairperson and five members.

questions.q: What is the term of office for the CAG?
questions.e: The CAG holds office for a period of six years.

questions.q: Who is the 'highest law officer' in the state?
questions.e: The Advocate General is the highest law officer in the state.

questions.q: The "Antyodaya" principle is associated with:
questions.e: Antyodaya is enunciated in Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay's idea of service to the poor.

questions.q: Who appoints the Solicitor General of India?
questions.e: While not explicitly in the summary, law officers of the Union are generally appointed by the President (Executive).

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "Audit Reports" of CAG?
questions.e: Article 151 deals with the audit reports of the CAG.

questions.q: The NITI Aayog follows which type of approach?
questions.e: NITI Aayog follows a bottom-up approach.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the NHRC?
o: Retired CJI or Supreme Court Judge
questions.e: The chairperson should be a retired chief justice of India or a judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The "Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat" deals with:
questions.e: It deals with matters related to marriage and family affairs.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the "Inter-State Council"?
questions.e: Article 263 deals with the Inter-State Council.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chairperson of the State Human Rights Commission?
questions.e: The chairperson and members of the SHRC are appointed by the Governor.

questions.q: The NCPCR operates under which ministry?
o: Ministry of Women and Child Development
questions.e: NCPCR operates under the administrative control of the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

questions.q: What is the retirement age of a High Court judge?
questions.e: High Court judges retire at the age of 62.

questions.q: Which Article provides for the "Attorney General"?
questions.e: Article 76 provides for the AG.

questions.q: The CAG submits reports related to the state to:
questions.e: The CAG submits reports related to state accounts to the Governor.

questions.q: Who is the 'guardian of public purse'?
questions.e: The CAG is the guardian of the public purse.

questions.q: The NITI Aayog was established in:
questions.e: NITI Aayog was established on January 1, 2015.

questions.q: Which Article is related to the "Finance Commission"?
questions.e: Article 280 is related to the Finance Commission.

questions.q: The "Team India Hub" in NITI Aayog represents:
questions.e: It carries out the mandate of fostering cooperative federalism with States.

questions.q: Who determines the salaries of NHRC members?
questions.e: The salaries are determined by the Central government.

questions.q: The NCW chairperson holds office for:
questions.e: The NCW chairperson and members hold office for three years.

questions.q: Which Article is related to "Official Language Commission"?
questions.e: Article 344 deals with the Official Language Commission.

questions.q: Who appoints the members of a Jails visiting team in NHRC?
questions.e: The commission (NHRC) has the function to visit jails and detention places.

questions.q: The CAG is the head of:
questions.e: The CAG is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.

questions.q: Which Article is related to "Election Commission"?
questions.e: Article 324 deals with the Election Commission.

questions.q: The "Knowledge and Innovation Hub" is part of:
questions.e: It is one of the two main hubs of NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Who appoints the Advocate General?
questions.e: The Advocate General is appointed by the Governor.

questions.q: What is the term of a High Court judge?
questions.e: A High Court judge holds office until they attain the age of 62 years.

questions.q: Which Article deals with "National Commission for SCs"?
questions.e: Article 338 deals with the NC SC.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the GST Council?
questions.e: The Union Finance Minister is the chairperson of the GST Council.

questions.q: The "Antyodaya" principle focuses on:
questions.e: Antyodaya focuses on the uplift of the poor and marginalised.

questions.q: Which Article provides for "Comptroller and Auditor General"?
questions.e: Article 148 provides for the CAG.

questions.q: Who is the highest law officer in India?
questions.e: The Attorney General is the highest law officer.

questions.q: The NHRC was established in:
questions.e: The NHRC was established in 1993.

questions.q: Who appoints the chairperson of the NCPCR?
questions.e: The Chairperson and members are appointed by the Central Government.

questions.q: The "Parivarik Mahila Lok Adalat" is associated with:
questions.e: It is an innovative concept evolved by the NCW.

questions.q: Which Article deals with "State Public Service Commission"?
questions.e: Article 315 deals with UPSC and SPSC.

questions.q: The "Demographic Dividend" principle is used by:
questions.e: It is one of the guiding principles of NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Who is the ex-officio member of NHRC from the NC Women?
questions.e: The chairperson of the National Commission for Women is an ex-officio member of NHRC.

questions.q: The NITI Aayog replaced:
questions.e: NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission.

questions.q: Which Article is related to "Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities"?
questions.e: Article 350-B deals with the Special Officer.

questions.q: Who appoints the Chief Minister of Delhi?
questions.e: The Chief Minister of Delhi is appointed by the President.

questions.q: What is the retirement age of a Supreme Court judge?
questions.e: SC judges retire at 65.

questions.q: The "Team India Hub" is part of:
questions.e: Team India Hub is one of the two hubs of NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Which Article is related to "Inter-State Council"?
questions.e: Article 263 is related to the Inter-State Council.

questions.q: Who determines the salary of the CAG?
questions.e: The salary of the CAG is determined by the Parliament.

questions.q: The "watchdog of human rights" in India is:
questions.e: NHRC is the watchdog of human rights.

questions.q: Which Article is related to "Attorney General"?
questions.e: Article 76 deals with the AG.

questions.q: The NCPCR consists of a chairperson and how many members?
questions.e: The NCPCR consists of a chairperson and six members.

questions.q: Who appoints the Governor of a state?
questions.e: The Governor is appointed by the President.

questions.q: What is the term of office for NCW members?
questions.e: NCW members hold office for three years.

questions.q: Which Article is related to "National Commission for Scheduled Tribes"?
questions.e: Article 338A deals with the NC ST.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of NITI Aayog?
questions.e: The Prime Minister is the chairperson of NITI Aayog.
